releases.name: scionwood 0.1.0
releases.body:
First release.

Worktrees for [opencode](https://opencode.ai) that pull down code you didn't write — each with its own index.

```bash
npm install -g scionwood
```

Then add `"scionwood"` to the `plugin` array in your global opencode config, and `wt --version` to check.

**What it does**

- `wt new audit --pr 1234` fetches a pull request into an isolated worktree. `prRef` makes the same flow work on GitLab, Gitea and Bitbucket.
- `wt new spike-auth`, `--from v2.1.0`, `--branch feat-x` for everything that isn't a PR.
- Each worktree gets its own tooling — its own code index, its own docker compose project — from a `tools` entry, no code.
- The plugin never invokes the model: no tool, no prompt injection, no slash commands. A test enforces it.
- `wt teardown` refuses to discard uncommitted changes or commits that exist nowhere else.

See the [README](https://github.com/selcukusta/scionwood#readme) and [docs/extending.md](https://github.com/selcukusta/scionwood/blob/main/docs/extending.md).
